title: An Incremental Approach to Compiler Construction
why: The canonical step-by-step build of a tiny compiler that emits real x86-64 assembly from the simplest expressions upward, ideal for the first hands-on chapter.

title: System V Application Binary Interface: AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement
why: The authoritative definition of x86-64 registers, stack frames, and the calling convention a code generator must follow on Linux.

title: Programming Techniques: Regular Expression Search Algorithm
why: Thompson's original construction turning a regular expression into an NFA, the theoretical basis of every regex-based lexer generator.

title: Regular Expression Matching Can Be Simple And Fast
why: A working engineer's readable walkthrough of Thompson NFA simulation versus backtracking, with runnable implementations.

title: Package go/scanner
why: Official documentation for a real hand-written production scanner, the concrete counterexample to generated lexers.

title: Top Down Operator Precedence
why: Pratt's original precedence-parsing method, the foundation of the expression parsers most production compilers use today.

title: Engineering a Compiler
why: A modern engineering-oriented textbook covering the full pipeline and, relevant here, context-free grammars, top-down and bottom-up parsing, and semantic analysis.

title: rust-analyzer syntax trees (docs/dev/syntax.md)
why: Describes a lossless, error-resilient syntax tree design in production tooling, the concrete model for the AST chapter.

title: Types and Programming Languages
why: The canonical textbook for chapter 7 typing rules, progress and preservation, subtyping and variance, and for chapter 8's Hindley-Milner reconstruction and Algorithm W (ch. 22-23).

title: Principal type-schemes for functional programs
why: The original paper defining Damas-Milner let-polymorphism and Algorithm W, the primary source for chapter 8's inference rules.

title: Generics implementation - GC Shape Stenciling
why: The Go team's own design explaining GC-shape stenciling plus dictionaries, why Go sits between full monomorphization and type erasure, and the itab/dictionary mechanics for chapter 9.

title: Efficiently Computing Static Single Assignment Form and the Control Dependence Graph
why: The original SSA paper defining dominance frontiers, minimal phi placement and renaming, and the dominance/dataflow framework for chapters 11 and 12.

title: Simple and Efficient Construction of Static Single Assignment Form
why: Presents the on-the-fly SSA construction algorithm that lowers an AST or bytecode directly to SSA without computing dominance frontiers, for chapter 12's alternative to Cytron.

title: LLVM Language Reference Manual
why: The authoritative spec of LLVM IR's SSA values, phi nodes, basic blocks and module structure, the reference for chapters 10 and 13.

title: Introduction to the Go compiler's SSA backend (cmd/compile/internal/ssa/README.md)
why: The Go compiler's own walkthrough of values, memory state, blocks/CFGs, the pass pipeline, rewrite rules, lowering and GOSSAFUNC, for chapters 10, 11 and 13.

title: Land ahoy: leaving the Sea of Nodes
why: V8 engineers explain what a Sea of Nodes IR is, why Turbofan used it, and why they replaced it with a CFG-based IR, the builder's write-up for chapter 13.

title: Alive2: Bounded Translation Validation for LLVM
why: Primary paper on bounded translation validation that checks whether an LLVM optimization is actually correct.

title: Taming Undefined Behavior in LLVM
why: Explains LLVM's undef/poison model and the freeze instruction, the design that defines how optimizations must treat UB.

title: Finding and Understanding Bugs in C Compilers
why: Introduces Csmith and differential testing, the standard method for fuzzing compilers and catching miscompilations.

title: Linear Scan Register Allocation
why: The original linear-scan algorithm, covering live intervals and spilling as a fast alternative to graph coloring.

title: Global Instruction Selection (GlobalISel) and The LLVM Target-Independent Code Generator
why: Official documentation for instruction selection (SelectionDAG, GlobalISel, TableGen) and the machine-level backend pipeline.

title: ELF and ABI Standards (ELF gABI specification)
why: Primary specification of ELF sections, symbols, relocations, and program loading used by linkers and loaders.

title: The Garbage Collection Handbook: The Art of Automatic Memory Management
why: The canonical reference for mark-sweep, copying, generational and concurrent collectors, stack maps and write barriers, and the one book to own for chapter 21's runtime/GC material.

title: A Guide to the Go Garbage Collector
version: describes the garbage collector as of Go 1.19 (living document)
why: Plain-language, implementation-specific account of Go's concurrent mark-sweep collector, its tri-color marking, GOGC tuning and the runtime's cost model.

title: Itanium C++ ABI: Exception Handling
why: The normative specification for zero-cost exception handling, the LSDA, call-site tables and the .eh_frame unwinding ABI used by GCC, Clang and Rust.

title: Optimizing Dynamically-Typed Object-Oriented Languages With Polymorphic Inline Caches
why: Original Self paper introducing polymorphic inline caches, the mechanism behind both modern IC-based dispatch and V8-style hidden classes.

title: Copy-and-Patch Compilation: A Fast Compilation Algorithm for High-Level Languages and Bytecode
why: The template-JIT technique that emits machine code at runtime by copying precompiled stencils and patching in operands, now used by CPython 3.13.

title: PEP 744 - JIT Compilation
why: First-hand design rationale for CPython's copy-and-patch JIT: adaptive interpreter and micro-ops tiers, why copy-and-patch, platform support and security (W^X) implications.

title: Introduction to the Go compiler (src/cmd/compile/README.md)
why: The gc compiler's own architecture tour, phase by phase from parsing through SSA to machine code, plus the practical flags for reading IR and SSA dumps.

title: Queries: demand-driven compilation (Rust Compiler Development Guide)
why: Explains rustc's memoized query system and dependency graph, the foundation the guide builds on to describe query-based incremental compilation.

title: Engineering a Compiler (2nd edition)
why: A readable copy of the course textbook used to quote its exact definitions of compiler and interpreter (the 3rd edition, S7, was not readable online).

title: Python 3.13 Glossary
why: Official definition of CPython bytecode and the virtual machine that executes it.

title: What's New In Python 3.13
why: Official account of CPython 3.13's experimental JIT: its build-time option, the Tier 1/Tier 2 IR architecture, and its use of copy-and-patch.

title: The javac Command (JDK 23)
why: Official description of what the javac tool produces.

title: Java Virtual Machine Technology Overview (Java SE 21 JVM Guide)
version: Java SE 21, Java Virtual Machine Guide F80256-03 (October 2025)
why: Oracle's description of HotSpot's adaptive compiler and how it compiles hot spots at run time.

title: The Architecture of Open Source Applications, Volume 1: LLVM
version: AOSA Volume 1 (2011), chapter 11, by Chris Lattner
why: Lattner's own account of LLVM's three-phase design and the retargetability argument for one shared optimizer across N source languages and M targets, plus the three forms of LLVM IR.

title: GNU Compiler Collection (GCC) Internals
why: The GCC project's own manual naming and describing its intermediate representations GENERIC, GIMPLE and RTL.

title: Using as: AT&T Syntax versus Intel Syntax (GNU assembler manual)
why: States the GNU assembler's default x86 syntax and the AT&T source-then-destination operand order needed to read the generated .s file.

title: PUSH — Push Word, Doubleword, or Quadword Onto the Stack
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Exact effect of PUSH on the stack pointer and memory, including the 64-bit operand size.

title: POP — Pop a Value From the Stack
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Exact effect of POP on the stack pointer and destination, including the 64-bit operand size.

title: IDIV — Signed Divide
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Dividend/quotient/remainder registers and the #DE divide-error conditions for signed division.

title: CWD/CDQ/CQO — Convert Word to Doubleword/Convert Doubleword to Quadword
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: The RAX-to-RDX sign extension that forms the wide dividend consumed by idiv.

title: Linux x86 trap handling (arch/x86/kernel/traps.c)
why: Shows that Linux turns the x86 #DE divide error into SIGFPE with si_code FPE_INTDIV.

title: Go 1.5 Release Notes
why: The primary release notes documenting the Go toolchain's move from C to Go and the resulting self-hosting build requirement.

title: Installing Go from source
why: Official statement of the minimum bootstrap Go compiler for each Go version and the general bootstrap version policy.

title: What Bootstrapping does - Rust Compiler Development Guide
why: Defines rustc's stage0/stage1/stage2 bootstrap stages and which compiler builds each stage.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust (Turing Award Lecture)
why: Thompson's own account of a compiler that reproduces a Trojan horse, the canonical source for the trust problem in bootstrapping.

title: Frequently Asked Questions — The Go Programming Language
why: Native compilation and inclusion of the Go runtime in standalone binaries.

title: Options Controlling the Kind of Output — GCC
why: Compilation, assembly, linking and the meanings of -c and -S.

title: Special Characters — GNU assembler x86 syntax
why: Semicolon instruction separators in the generated assembly.

title: Command-line Options — GNU linker
why: The meaning of a non-executable .note.GNU-stack section.

title: Options That Control Optimization — GCC 6.5.0
why: Explicit explanation of the C signed-overflow rule, not a claim about the lab's optimization flags.

title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Volume 1: Basic Architecture
why: The authoritative description of the x86-64 general-purpose register set, the operand-size zero-extension rule, little-endian byte order, and the Jcc condition-code table.

title: CMP — Compare Two Operands
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Exact statement of the status flags CMP sets and that it sets them in the same manner as SUB.

title: CALL — Call Procedure
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Exact behaviour of CALL: what is pushed as the return address and how the 64-bit operand size is forced.

title: RET — Return From Procedure
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Exact behaviour of RET: popping the return address into the instruction pointer and the 64-bit operation size.

title: LEA — Load Effective Address
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: States that LEA computes an effective address into a register and affects no flags.

title: LEAVE — High Level Procedure Exit
version: felixcloutier.com mirror of the Intel 64 and IA-32 SDM, viewed 2026-10-12
why: Exact behaviour of LEAVE and its fixed 64-bit operation size in 64-bit mode.

title: Using as: i386 Memory References (GNU assembler manual)
why: Gives the base+index*scale+disp memory operand and its AT&T spelling disp(base,index,scale), plus RIP-relative addressing on x86-64.

title: Go internal ABI specification (src/cmd/compile/abi-internal.md)
why: The Go team's own specification of ABIInternal: which registers pass integer arguments and results on amd64, how arguments are assigned, and how it differs from stack-based ABIs.

title: Go 1.17 Release Notes
why: The primary release notes announcing that Go 1.17 passes function arguments and results in registers on 64-bit x86 (and which ports it applies to).

title: x64 calling convention
why: Microsoft's authoritative description of the Windows x64 convention: integer argument registers RCX/RDX/R8/R9 and the caller-allocated shadow store, the contrast to System V.

title: Options That Control Optimization (GCC manual)
why: The current GCC manual's definitions of -O0/-O1/-O2 and of -fomit-frame-pointer, including the levels at which it is enabled.

title: Options for Code Generation Conventions (GCC manual)
why: The current GCC manual's definition of -fasynchronous-unwind-tables (and hence the -fno- form that suppresses the .cfi_ unwind tables).

title: objdump (GNU Binary Utilities)
why: The objdump manual: what -d disassembles and how the -M disassembler options select Intel versus AT&T syntax.

title: Compiler Explorer README
why: The project's own description of Compiler Explorer as an interactive compiler exploration website and its origin.

title: About me - Matt Godbolt
why: The creator's own statement of having released Compiler Explorer in 2012, the primary source for who made it.

title: MOVAPS — Move Aligned Packed Single Precision Floating-Point Values
why: Verifies the lab's 128-bit aligned memory store and its general-protection exception on misalignment.

title: Go runtime cgo call and callback support
why: Documents generated wrappers and runtime adapters on both Go-to-C and C-to-Go crossings.

title: MOV — Move
why: Verifies immediate-move encoding sizes.
